en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Darkness of Night, 20.
The Training Rule on Weeping.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, having quarreled with the bhikkhunīs, was weeping while repeatedly beating herself.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and grumbled, saying:
"How can the noble lady Caṇḍakāḷī weep while repeatedly beating herself?"... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī weeps, having repeatedly struck herself?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī weep after repeatedly beating herself?

This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence... And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, should beat herself with her own hand, whether once, twice, or thrice, this is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture."* (*The full rule continues with the standard formula for an offense of expiation involving forfeiture, including the allowance for a single stroke if it is done out of affection or for the purpose of healing a wound.)
“Whatever nun, however, should weep while repeatedly beating herself, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Herself" (attānaṃ):
"Privately.
Having struck her again and again, she weeps: there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
She strikes her but does not weep: there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If she weeps but does not scold, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if,
being afflicted by the loss of relatives, the loss of wealth, or the loss of health, she weeps but does not scold.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The second chapter: The Chapter on Darkness.
